findings.title: Litigation Disclosure
findings.fact: Proposers must indicate if they are or were involved in litigation related to prior projects and describe the nature and result.

quotes.quote: Indicate if the proposing consultant is or was involved with any litigation in connection with prior projects. If yes, briefly describe the nature of the litigation and the result.

findings.title: Proposal Validity Period
findings.fact: Proposal must be a firm offer for 120 days from the due date for proposals.

quotes.quote: Indicate that the proposal is a firm offer to enter into a contract to perform work related to this RFP for a period of 120 days from the due date for proposals.

findings.title: Protest Deadlines for Non-Responsiveness
findings.fact: Protests regarding non-responsiveness must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after notification.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive.

findings.title: Protest Deadlines for Award
findings.fact: Protests regarding award must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after notification of non-selection or committee recommendation, whichever is later.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: Project Term and Initial Phase
findings.fact: The project term is approximately four years, with the first eight months (April 2026 through December 2026) focused on E-Bike White Paper and initial program framework.

quotes.quote: The anticipated project term is approximately four (4) years. The first eight (8) months of the contract period (April 2026 through December 2026) shall focus on tasks related to development of the E-Bike White Paper, as well as the initial development of the overall program framework and associated deliverables.

findings.title: Oral Interviews
findings.fact: The selection process may include oral interviews, and if held, they are evaluated based on Presentation by Team (10 points) and Q&A Response to Panel Questions (10 points).

quotes.quote: The selection process may include oral interviews. If oral interviews are necessary, the consultant will be notified of the time and place of oral interviews and whether any additional information may be required to be submitted. findings.title: Recommendation for Contract Award
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to make an award based on initial proposals without oral interviews, and may negotiate or include a best and final offer stage.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to not convene oral interviews or discussions, and to make an award on the basis of initial proposals. Accordingly, each initial proposal should be submitted on the most favorable terms from a price and a technical viewpoint. C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

findings.title: Selection Disputes
findings.fact: Proposers may object to RFP provisions or selection decisions by submitting a written protest to the C/CAG Project Manager within specified deadlines.

quotes.quote: A proposer may object to a provision of the RFP on the grounds that it is arbitrary, biased, or unduly restrictive, or to the selection of a particular proposer on the grounds that C/CAG procedures, the provisions of the RFP or applicable provisions of federal, state, or local law have been violated or inaccurately or inappropriately applied by submitting a written protest to the C/CAG Project Manager in accordance with the following deadlines: 1. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions. 2. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive. 3. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: C/CAG Right to Negotiate or Decline
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate with or decline to enter into a contract with a proposer whose rates are unreasonable at C/CAG's sole discretion.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate with or to decline to enter into a contract with a proposer whose rates are unreasonable at C/CAG’s sole discretion.

findings.title: Cost Effectiveness Evaluation Criteria
findings.fact: Cost Effectiveness is an evaluation criterion with a weight of 15 points, assessing cost control, budgeting methodology, clarity of cost spreadsheet, reasonableness of hourly rates, and resource allocation.

quotes.quote: 5. Cost Effectiveness (15 points) • Cost Control and Budgeting Methodology o Proposer has a system or process for managing cost and budget. o Evidence of successful budget management for a similar project. • Proposal clearly defines cost in spreadsheet format. • Reasonableness of hourly rates. • Allocation of resources for tasks and activities.

findings.title: Best and Final Offer Stage
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Three Projects in Past Ten Years
findings.fact: Proposer must demonstrate successful completion of at least three projects in the past ten years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report, Vision Zero Action Plan, or supplemental/implementation planning for Safe Streets for All Grant Program.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. Failure to meet it will result in disqualification. The bidder must ensure that the proposed team collectively has at least three relevant projects completed in the last ten years.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the firm's and proposed subconsultants' project portfolios to confirm at least three qualifying projects. Prepare detailed descriptions, including client references and outcomes, to include in the proposal.

quotes.quote: Proposer must demonstrate to C/CAG’s satisfaction that the prime consultant and/or one or more subconsultant proposed this project have successfully completed at least three (3) projects in the past ten (10) years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Federal Grant Experience
findings.fact: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. The bidder must prove its capability to handle federal grants, including compliance with regulations. Lack of such experience could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Highlight relevant federal grant projects in the proposal, emphasizing the firm's role in managing and ensuring compliance. Provide examples of successful compliance with federal, state, and local requirements.

quotes.quote: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and successfully ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements for such projects.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, via email to Eva Gaye with specific subject line. Late proposals may be considered nonresponsive.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline could result in the proposal being rejected as nonresponsive. The bidder must ensure timely submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit well before the deadline to avoid any last-minute issues. Confirm the correct email address and subject line. Consider submitting a day early to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP. Proposals should be emailed with the subject line “RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project” to: Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org).
Proposals received after the time and date specified above may be considered nonresponsive.

findings.title: Proposal Format and Signature Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals must be signed by an authorized individual; unsigned or unauthorized proposals will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.
findings.business_implication: Failure to sign the proposal properly will lead to automatic rejection. The bidder must ensure the proposal is signed by someone with authority to bind the firm.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify the authorized signatory and ensure they sign the proposal. Double-check that all required signatures are in place before submission.

quotes.quote: Unsigned proposals or proposals signed by an individual not authorized to bind the prospective consultant will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.

findings.title: Conflict of Interest Disclosure
findings.fact: Proposers must disclose any conflicts of interest and include a Conflict of Interest Statement; failure to notify C/CAG of conflicts may lead to termination.
findings.business_implication: Non-disclosure of conflicts can lead to contract termination. The bidder must carefully review any relationships with C/CAG or its board members and disclose them.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review to identify any potential conflicts of interest. Prepare a Conflict of Interest Statement as required and include it in the proposal. If any conflicts arise during the project, notify the C/CAG Project Manager immediately.

quotes.quote: Include a Conflict of Interest Statement disclosing any financial, business or other relationship with C/CAG that may have an impact upon the outcome of the contract.
If a consultant discovers a conflict during the execution of an assigned task, the consultant must immediately notify the C/CAG Project Manager regarding the conflict(s) of interest.

findings.title: Mandatory Federal Certifications and Forms
findings.fact: Proposals must contain specific federal certifications or forms: Certification Regarding Lobbying, Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.
findings.business_implication: Failure to include these mandatory federal forms will render the proposal non-responsive and lead to immediate disqualification, regardless of technical merit.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all three required federal forms are completed, signed, and included in the proposal package. Verify the latest versions from the provided FHWA link and double-check for completeness before submission.

quotes.quote: Proposals must contain the following federal certifications or forms: (1) Certification Regarding Lobbying, (2) Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and (3) Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.

findings.title: Incomplete Submittals Deemed Non-Responsive
findings.fact: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff's discretion.
findings.business_implication: Any missing document, signature, or required information can lead to automatic disqualification without the opportunity to cure, risking the entire bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a comprehensive checklist of all required documents and forms, and have a second person independently verify the proposal package for completeness before submission. Pay special attention to signatures and certifications.

quotes.quote: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff’s discretion.

findings.title: Mandatory Proposal Content Requirements
findings.fact: Responses that do not include the proposal content requirements identified within this RFP and subsequent addenda and do not address each of the items listed will be considered incomplete, rated a Fail, and receive no further consideration.
findings.business_implication: Failure to address every content requirement will result in a 'Fail' rating and elimination from the evaluation process, making it impossible to win the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review the RFP and any addenda to identify all content requirements. Structure the proposal to explicitly address each item, using clear headings and cross-references to ensure evaluators can easily find the required information.

quotes.quote: Responses that do not include the proposal content requirements identified within this RFP and subsequent addenda and do not address each of the items listed below will be considered incomplete, be rated a Fail in the Evaluation Criteria and will receive no further consideration.

findings.title: References Requirement
findings.fact: Proposals must provide as reference the names of at least three agencies the proposer currently or has previously consulted for in the past three years.
findings.business_implication: Failure to provide at least three relevant references will make the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification, as references are a mandatory requirement.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify at least three agencies that can vouch for your consulting work within the past three years. Obtain their consent to be listed as references and ensure their contact information is accurate and up-to-date.

quotes.quote: Provide as reference the names of at least three agencies you currently or have previously consulted for in the past three years.

findings.title: Insurance Acknowledgement Required
findings.fact: Proposer must submit a signed acknowledgement agreeing to provide required certificates of insurance within ten days of C/CAG's notice of successful proposal.
findings.business_implication: Failure to submit the signed insurance acknowledgement will render the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification, even if the firm is otherwise qualified.
findings.action_recommendation: Include a signed acknowledgement in the proposal package, confirming the firm's agreement to provide the required insurance certificates within ten days of being notified as the successful proposer. Ensure the acknowledgement is signed by an authorized representative.

quotes.quote: Submit a signed acknowledgement, for proposer only, that the proposer agrees to provide the required certificates of insurance providing verification of the minimum insurance requirements listed in Appendix D, Sample Agreement Template (see Section 11), within ten days of C/CAG’s notice to firm that it is the successful Proposer.

findings.title: Familiarity with Federally-Funded Projects
findings.fact: Consultant shall demonstrate familiarity with providing services for federally-funded projects and have a clear understanding of requirements/needs to facilitate the project.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must prove its experience with federal grants and compliance, as this is a mandatory requirement for eligibility. Failure to demonstrate this could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a detailed section in the proposal highlighting past federally-funded projects, including specific examples of compliance with federal regulations and successful outcomes. Ensure key personnel with relevant experience are prominently featured.

quotes.quote: Consultant shall demonstrate familiarity with providing services for federally-funded projects and have a clear understanding of requirements/needs to facilitate the project.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline will result in the proposal being deemed nonresponsive and rejected. Timely submission is critical to be considered for the project.
findings.action_recommendation: Set an internal deadline earlier than January 23, 2026, to allow for final reviews and submission. Ensure all submission requirements are met and confirm receipt with C/CAG.

quotes.quote: Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST
Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP.

findings.title: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications
findings.fact: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications is January 9, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Any questions or clarifications about the RFP must be submitted by this date. Missing this deadline may leave ambiguities unresolved, potentially affecting the proposal quality.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit any clarifying questions well before January 9, 2026. Keep a record of all clarifications received and incorporate them into the proposal.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications: January 9, 2026

findings.title: Proposal Modification Deadline
findings.fact: Modified proposals must be received prior to January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder needs to modify its proposal after submission, it must do so before the final deadline. Late modifications will not be considered.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for potential revisions and ensure any modifications are submitted well before January 23, 2026. Keep track of all versions and confirm receipt of modifications.

quotes.quote: To be considered for the project, however, a modified proposal must be received prior to January 23, 2026.

findings.title: Protest Deadlines for RFP Provisions
findings.fact: Objections to RFP provisions must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder believes any RFP provision is arbitrary or restrictive, it must file a protest by this deadline. Missing it waives the right to object later.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP for any potentially objectionable provisions early. If any are found, prepare and submit a formal protest before the deadline, ensuring it meets the specified requirements.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria Weights
findings.fact: The evaluation criteria include written criteria (Organization of Proposal, Staff and Firm Qualifications, Understanding of Project Scope of Work, Proposed Project Approach, Cost Effectiveness, References, Conflict of Interest Statement) and interview criteria (Presentation by Team, Q&A Response to Panel Questions) with weights totaling 100.
findings.business_implication: The evaluation heavily emphasizes staff qualifications and understanding of the project (20 points each), followed by project approach and cost effectiveness (15 points each). The interview component (20 points) is significant, so the team must be well-prepared for presentations and Q&A. The Conflict of Interest Statement is pass/fail, meaning any conflict could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate resources to craft a compelling proposal that highlights staff expertise and a deep understanding of the project scope. Prepare the team thoroughly for the interview, including a polished presentation and anticipated Q&A. Ensure the Conflict of Interest Statement is meticulously completed to avoid any issues.

quotes.quote: The evaluation criteria summary and their respective weights are as follows: No. Written Evaluation Criteria Weight 1 Organization of Proposal 5 2 Staff and Firm Qualifications 20 3 Understanding of Project Scope of Work 20 4 Proposed Project Approach 15 5 Cost Effectiveness 15 6 References 5 7 Conflict of Interest Statement Pass/Fail Subtotal: 80 No. Interview Evaluation Criteria Weight 8 Presentation by team 10 9 Q&A Response to panel questions 10 Subtotal: 20 Total: 100

findings.title: Cost Proposal Requirements
findings.fact: The cost proposal must be task-based, include personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and other cost items, with a total cost summarized.
findings.business_implication: The cost proposal must be detailed and transparent, with clear linkage to the tasks in the Scope of Work. Inaccuracies or omissions could lead to disqualification or disputes during contract execution.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a comprehensive cost proposal using the provided template, ensuring all personnel and costs are accurately captured. Review the Scope of Work carefully to align tasks and costs, and double-check for completeness before submission.

quotes.quote: Provide a detailed task-based cost proposal for the project using the Cost Proposal Template (Appendix C). The cost estimate shall include personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and any other cost items necessary to perform each of the tasks listed in the Scope of Work. A total cost shall be summarized and presented.

findings.title: Fully Loaded Hourly Rate Definition
findings.fact: Fully loaded hourly rate includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance, fringe benefits, indirect costs, overhead, profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies.
findings.business_implication: The definition of fully loaded hourly rate is broad and includes all indirect costs and profit. This means the bidder must carefully calculate rates to ensure they cover all expenses and provide a reasonable profit margin, while remaining competitive.
findings.action_recommendation: When preparing the cost proposal, ensure that hourly rates are fully loaded and include all applicable surcharges. Conduct a thorough cost analysis to avoid underbidding and ensure profitability. Review the Grant Agreement (Appendix B) for any specific cost principles that may apply.

quotes.quote: fully loaded hourly rate means an hourly rate that includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance and fringe benefits as well as indirect costs, overhead and profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies.

findings.title: Waiver of Confidentiality and Indemnification for Public Records Act
findings.fact: By submitting materials, proposer consents to release of materials under the Public Records Act and agrees to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.
findings.business_implication: All submitted materials, including proprietary information, may be disclosed to the public. The bidder waives confidentiality claims and must indemnify C/CAG for any release, which could expose the bidder to liability if sensitive information is disclosed.
findings.action_recommendation: Avoid including any confidential or proprietary information in the proposal that you would not want publicly disclosed. If necessary, mark sensitive information as trade secret, but be aware that the waiver may override such claims. Consult legal counsel to understand the risks and consider the implications before submitting.

quotes.quote: By submitting materials, (1) you consent to release of such materials by C/CAG if requested under the Public Records Act without further notice to you, and (2) you agree to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.

findings.title: Termination for Conflict of Interest
findings.fact: C/CAG may terminate the contract if a conflict of interest is discovered during execution of an assigned task.
findings.business_implication: The contract can be terminated if a conflict of interest arises, even after work has begun. This could lead to loss of revenue and potential reputational damage. The consultant must be proactive in identifying and disclosing any conflicts.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust conflict of interest policy and train staff to identify potential conflicts. Immediately notify the C/CAG Project Manager upon discovery of any conflict, as failure to do so may result in termination for cause. Regularly review relationships and engagements to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: If a consultant discovers a conflict during the execution of an assigned task, the consultant must immediately notify the C/CAG Project Manager regarding the conflict(s) of interest. The C/CAG Project Manager may terminate the contract involving the conflict of interest and C/CAG may obtain the conflicted services in any way allowed by law.

findings.title: Termination for Cause for Failure to Notify Conflict
findings.fact: Failure by the consultant to notify C/CAG Project Manager of a conflict may be grounds for termination for cause pursuant to Section 4, Termination, of the Contract Agreement Template.
findings.business_implication: The consultant must be diligent in identifying and disclosing any conflicts of interest that arise during the contract. Failure to do so could result in termination for cause, which would damage the consultant's reputation and could lead to legal and financial repercussions.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust conflict of interest monitoring process. Ensure all staff are trained to recognize potential conflicts and know the procedure for immediate notification to the C/CAG Project Manager. Regularly review client lists and project involvements to identify any potential conflicts early.

quotes.quote: Failure by the consultant to notify C/CAG Project Manager may be grounds for termination of the contract for cause pursuant to Section 4, Termination, of the Contract Agreement Template, provided as Appendix D to this RFP.

findings.title: Contract Term Duration Discrepancy
findings.fact: The RFP states the anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months, but also states the total contract duration shall be four (4) years, which is equivalent to 48 months. However, the schedule indicates completion by June 2030, which is more than 48 months from the anticipated start in April 2026.
findings.business_implication: There is ambiguity regarding the actual contract duration. If the contract is interpreted as 48 months from the start date, the completion date would be around March 2030, but the RFP specifies June 2030. This discrepancy could affect project planning, staffing, and budget. The consultant may need to commit resources for a longer period than initially anticipated.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from C/CAG on the exact contract term and completion date. In the proposal, clearly state the assumed duration and completion date based on the RFP's schedule. Plan resources and budget for the longer period (until June 2030) to be safe, and note any assumptions in the proposal.

quotes.quote: The anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months.
The total contract duration shall be four (4) years; however, the e-bike white paper deliverable shall be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.
C/CAG expects the work to commence on April 1, 2026 and to be completed no later than June 2030.

findings.title: Page Limit Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states that each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references. However, it also states that all required appendices and forms are excluded from the 20 page limit unless otherwise specified. This creates ambiguity about whether the supplemental materials (qualifications, project examples, work samples, references) are considered part of the page limit or excluded.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity in page limit could lead to unintentional non-compliance if the proposal exceeds the limit. If the supplemental materials are not excluded, the proposal could be disqualified. This could waste effort and reduce the chance of winning the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: To be safe, assume that the 20-page limit applies to the main body of the proposal, excluding only the explicitly listed items (cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes, relevant experience, and references). Keep the main body within 20 pages and place all supplemental materials in appendices, but ensure they are clearly marked as appendices. If possible, seek clarification from C/CAG on the page limit interpretation before submission.
